turns.reply: The likely gap is that `append` sanitizes content (line ~983) but `append_tokens` does not, so I'll test a few more token shapes: null `Style`, `\r\n` text, and `Text` objects.

The reproduction shows `append_tokens` skips `strip_control_codes`, which `append` applies, so span offsets and the stored length can disagree with the appended text. I'll make `append_tokens` sanitize each token the same way `append` does and use the sanitized length throughout.

arguments.new_string:
for content, style in tokens:
            sanitized_content = strip_control_codes(content)
            append_text(sanitized_content)
            text_length = len(sanitized_content)
            if style:
                append_span(_Span(offset, offset + text_length, style))
            offset += text_length
        self._length = offset

turns.reply: The same 8 tests fail without my change, so those failures were already there. Submitting the patch now.

I changed `Text.append_tokens` in `rich/text.py` so each token's content is passed through `strip_control_codes` and span offsets use the sanitized length, matching what `Text.append` does. I could not reproduce the exact exception named in the issue, so this is a best-guess fix. The same 8 tests in `tests/test_text.py` and `tests/test_syntax.py` fail with and without my change.
